```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A carries a regulatory burden that Idea B does not. A handles PHI, so it requires BAAs, a risk assessment and audited infrastructure from day one. The brief cites a year-one HIPAA compliance cost of $8,000-$25,000, which is hard to fit into a solo, 90-day path to a first paying customer.",
    "Idea B's demand evidence matches the proposed product. Three independent threads (dev.to, r/SaaS, r/Backend) describe production incidents from silent or short-notice upstream API changes. Idea A's own brief admits its sourced complaints are about incumbent pricing and group-practice friction, not an unmet need for a minimal notes and reminders app.",
    "Idea B has a cheap, self-serve billing channel. A GitHub Marketplace listing is free to list, and GitHub App distribution lets one operator ship and charge without a sales team. Idea A's main paid channel (Capterra PPC) has a $500/mo minimum, and its free channel (r/therapists) is limited by self-promotion norms.",
    "Both ideas face crowded markets. Idea B at least has a sourced competitor charging $29/mo (apidrift.co), which anchors a price point. Idea A must displace entrenched EHRs with high switching costs, plus $8/mo reminder-only tools."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's claim that SimplePractice has raised prices annually since its 2024 private-equity acquisition, and that this is driving switching interest, is sourced only to a competitor's marketing blog (upheal.io/blog/why-therapists-switch-to-upheal). That source has an obvious interest in the claim. The 'expensive for what it offers' quote likewise comes from another competitor's blog (oasys.health). The TheraSoft ($69) and TheraFocus ($199) prices have no source at all, and the $29 SimplePractice Starter tier is attributed only to unnamed 'third-party sources'.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B wins mainly because A has a heavy compliance burden and its demand evidence does not match the product, not because B is strong. B faces at least six shipping competitors, several of them free, and neither brief shows that any competitor has paying customers. B's CAC figure comes from a source flagged for a prompt-injection attempt and was treated as directional only."
}
```
